chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn Sama'ah, from Safwan, from 'Asim ibn Humayd, from Muhammad ibn Qays, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:
"There is no pledge (rahn) unless it is taken into possession."

key_terms.رَهْنَ: Pledge or collateral; an item given as security for a debt.
key_terms.مَقْبُوضًا: Taken into possession; physically held or controlled by the creditor.

ai.seo_question: What is the condition for a valid pledge (rahn) in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This concise hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) establishes the necessity of actual physical possession (qabd) for the validity of a pledge (rahn), a principle that distinguishes Shia jurisprudence from some other schools which may accept constructive possession. It underscores the importance of tangible security in commercial transactions to prevent disputes, reflecting the broader Islamic legal emphasis on clarity and the removal of ambiguity (gharar) in contracts.
